audit.whatIsWrong: The entry calls the reflect her R. It is her W. 'Mel's active R reflect', 'her R reflect punishes your all-in' and 'Hold her R reflect' all point the player at the wrong button, and one of the four spike rows is labelled 'Her R window'.
audit.why: Riot's text: Rebuttal (W) 'forms a barrier around herself that reflects enemy projectiles back at the attacker, prevents her from taking damage, and grants her movement speed' on 38/35/33/29/26. Golden Eclipse (R) is something else entirely: 'Mel strikes all enemies marked with Overwhelm regardless of their distance from her, dealing additional damage for each stack of Overwhelm', 120/100/80. A player waiting for 'her R' to drop before committing is watching a 120-second global while the 38-second barrier that actually blocks them comes back four times as often.
audit.corrected: Every reflect reference now names Rebuttal (W) with its 38s rank-1 cooldown, the spike label is 'Her W window', and Golden Eclipse is described for what it does.

audit.whatIsWrong: The advice is to avoid dumping your slam into the reflect because it 'bounces your own burst back'. Nothing Ambessa casts can be reflected.
audit.why: Rebuttal reflects projectiles. None of Ambessa's five abilities is a projectile — Cunning Sweep and Sundering Slam are a semicircle and a line she swings, Repudiation is a self-centred slam, Lacerate whips around her, Public Execution is a blink. What Rebuttal actually does to her is the other clause: it prevents damage outright and speeds Mel up. Bait it for the right reason and the timing is the same; bait it for the wrong reason and the player will also fear casting things that were never at risk.
audit.corrected: spikes[3].text, mid, late and wants.foe[1] now say damage prevention, not reflection.

audit.whatIsWrong: Golden Eclipse and Searing Brilliance are absent from the whole entry, so the level-6 row and the late game are both explained by the wrong ability.
audit.why: Riot's text on Searing Brilliance: 'When Mel deals damage through an ability or attack, she applies Overwhelm, which can stack infinitely. If the enemy is hit by Mel with enough Overwhelm damage, the stacks are consumed to execute the target.' Golden Eclipse then 'strikes all enemies marked with Overwhelm regardless of their distance from her'. Poke you shrug off in lane is stored, and at 6 she can cash it from anywhere on the map. That is why the chart gives her level 6 even though your ultimate is the better duel tool.
audit.corrected: whys[4] and late now explain the stage with Golden Eclipse, and breakdown.cooldowns carries its 120s.
sources: champ-data/_kits/mel.json (P Searing Brilliance, R Golden Eclipse)

audit.whatIsWrong: Her two lane abilities are only ever 'her Q poke' and 'her E', with no ranges and no cooldowns, in a matchup whose entire difficulty is whether you can walk at her.
audit.why: Radiant Volley is 950 range on 10/9/8/7/6 and Solar Snare is 1000 range on 11/10.5/10/9.5/9, rooting at the centre and slowing around it. Ambessa's longest reach before 6 is Cunning Sweep at 650. The gap between 1000 and 650 is the lane, and the root is the only thing that stops the walk-up.
audit.corrected: Named with ranges and cooldowns in spikes[0].text, whys[0], whys[1], whys[3], wants.foe[0], wants.foe[2], breakdown.cooldowns and phases[1].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Your R passive armor-pen plus on-ability-hit healing eats her poke during the dive' in mid, repeated in spikes[2].text and whys[5].
audit.why: Riot's Public Execution text has no penetration, no healing and no passive: 'blinks to the farthest enemy champion in a line of her choosing and suppresses them upon her arrival. She then slams the enemy into the ground where they take damage and are stunned.' The kit file's derived 'heal' flag on her R contradicts the description it came from. What actually makes the dive work is the suppression — a suppressed Mel cannot cast Rebuttal.
audit.corrected: Replaced in mid, spikes[1].text, spikes[2].text, wants.you[0] and whys[5].

edits.before: You own the straight 1v1 through your item spikes, but Mel is a scaling poke mage — if the game drags, full-build she pokes you down from max range before you reach her, and her R reflect punishes your all-in commit. Your entire combo is physical, so her R reflect plus a Zhonya's or Banshee and distance from her team blunt your dive. Close the lane on your power curve, snowball off your 6 and first-item windows, and don't let a fed Mel turn a teamfight into a poke-and-reflect war where her range and your reflected burst both work against you.
edits.after: You own the straight 1v1 through your item spikes, but Mel is a scaling poke mage — full-build she pokes you down from 950 before you reach her, and Rebuttal blanks your commit for its whole duration. Golden Eclipse then strikes every Overwhelm stack she has banked on you from anywhere on the map, so chip you shrugged off in lane is damage she saves for the teamfight. Close the lane on your power curve, snowball off your 6 and first-item windows, and never let a fed Mel turn the game into a poke war her range wins.

notes: The load-bearing error here was a slot mix-up: the reflect barrier is Rebuttal (W) on 38s, not her R, and Golden Eclipse — a 120s effectively global strike on every Overwhelm stack she has put on you — was missing from the entry entirely. The knock-on is that the player was told to wait out the wrong cooldown before committing. Rebuttal also cannot reflect anything Ambessa casts: she has no projectile on any slot, so what matters is its damage prevention. Public Execution was again credited with armour penetration and healing it does not have. Sides and ratings already agree with the completed mirror at audits/top/mel__ambessa.json (Mel, Skill, Ambessa, Ambessa, Mel, Ambessa, Ambessa) so I changed neither. The mirror auditor also traced the fabricated 'Dash Chain' Ambessa ability to a single table row in champ-data/_gen-engine.js — worth fixing at source, since 'Dash Chain' still appears across roughly 30 champ-data files that generated Ambessa matchups.
